items.description: The requirement 'Explainer Grounding and Coverage Disclosure' mandates that 'Every reply SHALL end with exactly one disclosure line: Grounding: graph @ <sha7>; ... when grounded ..., or Grounding: source read, unverified (<reason>) when not, where <reason> is one of graph stale, graph absent, graph check failed, symbol not in graph, or form not graph-backed', and scenario 'Disclosure line present on every answer' requires that every reply end with a Grounding: line. However, scenario 'Ambiguous symbol asks instead of guessing' requires the skill to list candidate IDs and ask which symbol was meant without reading source or sketching a tree, and scenario 'Whole-repository question redirected' redirects to /codebase-atlas and stops. For these replies, source was not read, and none of the five allowed <reason> tokens represents an ambiguous symbol clarification prompt or a tool redirect. The disclosure requirement and scenario set contradict the clarification and redirection flows.

Requirement 'Explainer Grounding and Coverage Disclosure' lacks a normative SHALL/MUST statement specifying how the skill handles exit code 3 (ambiguous target) from build_atlas.py --tree, even though scenario 'Ambiguous symbol asks instead of guessing' specifies that the skill SHALL list candidate ids from stderr and ask which one was meant instead of falling back to source reading. The requirement body should explicitly specify the ambiguous symbol handling contract.

Requirement 'Atlas Symbol Tree Export' specifies that --hops N has a maximum of 4 and that 'larger values clamped with a stderr note', that --no-coverage suppresses the coverage footer, and that exit code 1 is used for input or IO errors. None of these behaviors has a corresponding scenario with WHEN/THEN in the specification, violating Rule Group 2's requirement that every SHALL/MUST requirement has at least one scenario.

In requirement 'Explainer Grounding and Coverage Disclosure', the grounded disclosure template Grounding: graph @ <sha7>; <language> <percent>% / <language> <percent>% covered states in parentheses '(coverage list copied verbatim from the --tree footer after its · separator, including order and / separators)'. Because the footer from specs/codebase-analysis/spec.md already ends with ' covered', verbatim copying after '· ' would duplicate the trailing ' covered'. As properly specified in design D5, the specification should state that the coverage list is copied after '· ' and before the trailing ' covered'.

In design D5, 'graph stale' is defined as 'run_architecture.py --check exited non-zero'. However, D2 and the live contract define exit 1 specifically as stale provenance while other non-zero exits are execution or script failures ('graph check failed'). Defining 'graph stale' as any non-zero exit in D5 creates an internal inconsistency with D2.

The diff closes the ungrounded reason set to exactly five values (`graph stale`, `graph absent`, `graph check failed`, `symbol not in graph`, `form not graph-backed`) and simultaneously adds the 'Ambiguous symbol asks instead of guessing' scenario. That reply contains no call tree and no catalogue form, yet 'Disclosure line present on every answer' still requires every reply to end with exactly one `Grounding:` line. None of the five reasons is valid for the ask reply: `symbol not in graph` is false (the symbol exists, that is the whole point of exit 3), `form not graph-backed` is false (no form was used), and the grounded form is forbidden. The same hole applies to the whole-repository redirect reply ('name /codebase-atlas and stop'). D5 in design.md has the identical closed list ('exactly one of'), and task 2.2 tests that the reference contains only this set, so an implementer cannot add a sixth reason without failing the deterministic test. Either add explicit reasons (e.g. `ambiguous symbol, awaiting choice` and `redirected to /codebase-atlas`) to D5, the spec requirement, task 2.2 and the grounding reference, or amend 'Disclosure line present on every answer' to exempt clarification and redirect replies.

D2 now states that `run_architecture.py --check` returns `1` when provenance is not fresh and that 'other failures are also non-zero'. D5 then asks the skill to emit `graph stale` for 'exited non-zero' and `graph check failed` for 'could not run (error/exception)', and the spec scenario says 'as appropriate'. With the contract as documented, an exit `1` from a traceback and an exit `1` from stale provenance are indistinguishable to the skill, so the two reasons cannot be told apart deterministically; `graph stale` as written ('exited non-zero') also subsumes `graph check failed`. Two further cases have no mapping at all: `--check` exits `0` but `build_atlas.py --tree` itself exits `1` (input/IO error on the graph), and the graph file is missing but `--check` still runs (does the skill stat the file before calling `--check`, or rely on the exit code?). Pin a decision rule in D5/grounding.md (e.g. `graph absent` when the skill's own existence check on the script or graph fails, run before `--check`; `graph check failed` when the subprocess cannot be spawned or `--tree` exits `1`; `graph stale` for every other non-zero `--check` exit) or collapse `stale` and `check failed` into one reason so the disclosure is decidable.

D4 still relies on `--check` and `--tree` never combining to keep exit `2` unambiguous, but neither the codebase-analysis requirement nor task 1.3 requires `build_atlas.py` to reject `--check --tree X` (argparse mutually exclusive group or an explicit exit-1 usage error with a scenario). As written the combination is undefined and exit `2` could mean 'stale page' or 'not found' depending on dispatch order. Ledger id 8 flagged this and is marked addressed without a change.

The spec says the copied span is everything 'after its `· ` separator' (which includes the trailing word `covered`), while design D5 says the span is 'after `· ` and before the trailing ` covered`' with `covered` then re-appended. The resulting strings are identical, but the two documents describe different substrings, and task 2.2's deterministic test will be written against one of them. Pick one phrasing and use it in both D5 and the spec.

The spec now says 'exactly one decimal place as `Coverage.percent` returns it', and D3 says 'never re-rounded'. This still assumes `Coverage.percent` already yields a one-decimal value; the packet does not include the `Coverage` definition. If it returns an unrounded float, 'exactly one decimal' and 'never re-rounded' conflict. Pinning the format expression (`f"{coverage.percent:.1f}"`) in D3 and stating that the page banner uses the same expression removes the ambiguity. Ledger id 10 marked addressed; residual risk is low if task 1.1's footer-equality test is written against the banner's rendered string rather than the raw float.

Proposal Tests bullet (1) still says the deterministic check verifies 'both D5 disclosure forms', while task 2.2 and D7 item 1 were widened in this same revision to require the full ungrounded reason set. Minor drift introduced by this iteration; the proposal is the document Gate reviewers read first.

The whole-repository scenario requires the skill to name `/codebase-atlas` “and stop,” while the grounding requirement and D5 require every reply, without exception, to end with exactly one `Grounding:` line. The redirect response therefore has two incompatible required endings. Specify whether redirects append the disclosure or are an explicit exception.

Proposal.md and task 1.1 say the atlas test proves output contains only fixture node ids, but the specified tree format prints node names, file locations, and kinds—not node ids. That assertion is not implementable as written and cannot establish the claimed no-invented-symbol guarantee. Define a validation based on emitted node tuples or include stable ids in the output contract.

The Atlas Symbol Tree Export requirement contains SHALL clauses with no corresponding WHEN/THEN coverage: default hop/direction behavior; clamping hops above 4 with a stderr note; exact `<name> (<file>:<line>) [<kind>]` formatting; secondary sorting by id; `--no-coverage` suppression; unique-name and full-path resolution plus resolution precedence; exit 1 for input/IO errors; and the standard-library/no-network constraint. Add scenarios covering these obligations or move non-behavioral implementation guidance out of normative SHALL language.

The skill-workflow specs also leave normative clauses without explicit scenario coverage. In particular, no scenario asserts that the skill does not open a browser, that `triggers:` is absent, that `SKILL.md` ends with all three required tail sections, or that the manifest contains the exact `portable` distribution and exact dependency list. Existing scenarios cover adjacent behavior but not these stated SHALL/SHALL NOT contracts.

The grounding spec says the coverage list is copied verbatim from the tree footer “after its `·` separator,” which includes the footer’s trailing `covered`, while the grounded disclosure template itself also ends in `covered`. D5 instead defines the copied span as after `· ` and before the trailing ` covered`. Align the normative spec with D5 to prevent implementations from producing `covered covered` or interpreting “verbatim” inconsistently.

D5 / proposal / tasks still leave a disclosure-format gap for grounded call trees: design says the disclosure copies the --tree footer coverage list verbatim (language order, ` / ` separators, one-decimal percents) but uses `; ` after the sha and `Grounding:` prefix, while the grounded example and older proposal language still risk drift if implementers treat the whole footer as copy-paste. More importantly, D7 deterministic check #1 and proposal Tests bullet only require that D5 strings / both disclosure forms appear in the grounding reference — they do not require asserting the closed ungrounded reason enum (`graph stale`, `graph absent`, `graph check failed`, `symbol not in graph`, `form not graph-backed`) nor the footer→disclosure mapping (`;` vs `·`). Task 2.5 was supposedly updated per plan-findings #2, but the contracted CI checks remain string-presence only, so a wrong reason token or footer/disclosure drift can still pass.

Ambiguous-symbol path (exit 3) is specified in design D4 and a skill-workflow scenario, but the proposal 'What Changes' / Tests section and D7's three deterministic CI checks do not encode any assertion that SKILL.md/workflow instructs ask-don't-guess on exit 3 (list stderr candidates, no source fallback). Without a prompt-level check, implementers can ship the atlas exit code and still omit the skill branch, and plan-findings iteration 1 did not call this out.

D3 footer format is now precise (`graph @ <sha7> · python 14.4% / sql 37.0% covered`, sorted languages, one decimal, never re-rounded), and D5 says disclosure copies that coverage list verbatim after `; `. The grounded disclosure example correctly shows one-decimal percents, but D7 check #1 still phrases success as 'D5 strings present' without requiring the one-decimal / sorted-language / no-re-round rules to appear in the grounding reference or atlas tree tests. Acceptable residual risk if task 1.x atlas tests pin format; still a mild plan completeness gap between D3 precision and D7 check surface.

D5 reason `graph check failed` is defined as '`--check` could not run (error/exception)' while `graph stale` is 'run_architecture.py --check exited non-zero'. Live contract clarification says the script returns 1 when provenance is not fresh and other failures are also non-zero — so a non-zero exit alone cannot distinguish stale vs check-failed. Design does not say how the skill classifies stderr/exception vs exit code for those two reasons, yet both appear in the closed reason set the skill must emit exactly. Implementers may invent heuristics or collapse them, breaking the 'exactly one of' contract.

Requirement 'Explainer Frontmatter Without Triggers' contains normative obligations that lack Scenario coverage: 'The SKILL.md SHALL end with the ## Common Rationalizations, ## Red Flags, and ## Verification sections required of user-invocable skills' and 'SHALL NOT declare a triggers: key'. Neither of the requirement's two scenarios ('Frontmatter valid in both orderings' and 'Description carries the trigger condition') asserts the presence of the three required tail sections or verifies the absence of triggers:, violating Rule Group 2's requirement that every SHALL/MUST have at least one scenario.

Requirement 'Atlas Symbol Tree Export' contains normative SHALL obligations that lack Scenario coverage under Rule Group 2: (1) 'Each line SHALL show <name>  (<file>:<line>)  [<kind>]', (2) 'children SHALL be sorted by name then id' (secondary sort by id is omitted from scenarios), and (3) '<target> SHALL resolve as exact node id, then unique symbol name...' (existing scenarios cover node id and module basename, but no scenario verifies resolving a unique bare symbol name).

Design D7 and task 2.2 define three deterministic behavioural checks in test_behaviour.py, and task 2.2 lists scenario 'Ambiguous symbol asks instead of guessing' as covered. However, none of the three checks asserts that SKILL.md or references/grounding.md instructs the skill to ask rather than guess when --tree exits 3 (listing stderr candidate ids without source fallback). Check 1 only verifies that clarification and redirect replies are exempt from Grounding:. An implementation that omits the exit 3 prompt instructions would pass all three deterministic checks.

Requirement 'Explainer Grounding and Coverage Disclosure' specifies that if build_atlas.py --tree exits 1 after a fresh --check, the skill SHALL fall back to source reading and emit disclosure reason 'graph check failed'. However, scenario 'Stale or absent graph falls back to source' only triggers WHEN run_architecture.py --check exits non-zero or the script/graph file is missing, leaving the post-fresh --tree exit 1 failure branch without scenario coverage.

In .review-ledger/ledger.json, item 15 (uncovered normative clauses in skill-workflow/spec.md including triggers absence and required tail sections) is recorded as status 'addressed' by 'plan-review-adjudication'. However, plan-findings.md's adjudication table omitted item 15 and no corresponding scenarios were added to skill-workflow/spec.md, resulting in an unaddressed finding prematurely marked addressed in the ledger.

Design D4 notes that build_atlas.py --check uses exit 2 for a stale HTML page and states that '--check and --tree never combine on one invocation.' However, neither codebase-analysis/spec.md nor task 1.3 requires parse_args() in build_atlas.py to enforce mutual exclusivity (e.g. via an argparse mutually exclusive group). If both flags are passed, the meaning of exit code 2 is ambiguous.

Rule Group 2 (every SHALL/MUST has a WHEN/THEN scenario) is still violated in skill-workflow: (a) 'SHALL NOT declare a `triggers:` key' has no scenario — 'Frontmatter valid in both orderings' only asserts the six present keys; (b) 'SHALL end with the `## Common Rationalizations`, `## Red Flags`, and `## Verification` sections' has no scenario; (c) 'SHALL declare `"explain-code": {"distribution": "portable"}` and cross_skill_dependencies `[codebase-atlas, refresh-architecture]`' is only covered by 'Manifest validation passes' (zero errors), which does not assert the exact entries; (d) 'SHALL NOT open a browser' is only indirectly covered by 'SHALL NOT create, modify, or open any file'. Ledger item 15 records exactly this and is marked `addressed`, but no scenario was added and the adjudication table in plan-findings.md does not list id 15. Add scenarios (triggers absent → test fails if present; tail sections present; manifest entry equals the literal) or demote the clauses to non-normative text.

All 20 ledger items are stamped `status: addressed` / `addressed_by: plan-review-adjudication`, but the PLAN_REVIEW adjudication table in plan-findings.md only records resolutions for ids 1, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 12, 13, 14, 16, 17, 20. Ids 8 (`--check --tree` combination undefined), 15 (skill-workflow SHALLs without scenarios), 18 (no deterministic check for ask-don't-guess) and 19 (D7 does not require one-decimal/sorted rules) have no matching artifact change in this diff, and ids 2, 4, 10, 11 were fixed but not recorded. A round-2 converge will therefore re-raise 8/15/18 against a ledger that claims they are closed, and the audit trail cannot show why. Either apply the fixes or set those items to `open`/`accepted` with a resolution note in plan-findings.md.

The first-match reason order places `form not graph-backed` last, while the same requirement says 'other catalogue forms SHALL use `form not graph-backed`' and that freshness is determined 'before sketching a call tree'. If the skill runs the preflight/`--check` for a sequence-diagram question (nothing forbids it), first-match yields `graph absent` or `graph stale` for a reply where the graph was never consulted, contradicting the SHALL. If it does not run the check, the order is irrelevant for those forms but the spec never says the check is skipped. D5 has the same ordering. State explicitly that the form decision precedes the graph pipeline: non-call-tree forms skip `--check`/`--tree` and always emit `form not graph-backed`; the first-match order applies only within the call-tree path.

D7 deterministic check #1, task 2.2 and the proposal Tests bullet now assert the clarification/redirect *disclosure exemption*, but nothing asserts the ask-don't-guess behaviour itself (on `--tree` exit `3`: list stderr candidates, ask, no source fallback, no tree). Task 2.5 writes that rule into grounding.md but no CI check reads it back, so an implementer can ship exit 3 in the atlas and omit the skill branch and every deterministic test stays green. Ledger id 18 raised this and is marked addressed without a change.

Scenario 'Non-call edges are excluded' asserts `B` appears under a `callees:` heading for `--direction both`, but the requirement's line format (`<name>  (<file>:<line>)  [<kind>]`, footer) never defines section headings or how `--direction both` lays out callers vs callees. The scenario tests a string the normative text does not require, and byte-identical determinism (task 1.1) will be pinned against an undefined layout. Either add the `callers:` / `callees:` section rule for `both` to the requirement or drop the heading from the scenario.

The committed converge result embeds a machine-specific absolute `checkpoint_dir` (user home + worktree path) and a truncated raw vendor error payload. Harmless for the change, but it is a non-portable artifact under `openspec/changes/` that will be archived verbatim; the ledger alongside it is already the durable record. Consider recording a repo-relative checkpoint path or leaving converge-result.json out of the commit.

The “Narrow question answered with the smallest visual” scenario requires exactly one visual whenever a user asks about a specific function, module, or message path, but the ambiguous-symbol scenario forbids sketching a tree and requires a clarification question. A narrow request naming an ambiguous function satisfies both WHEN clauses and receives contradictory outcomes. Qualify the first scenario to cover resolvable targets or explicitly exempt ambiguity clarification.

The “No file or browser side effects” scenario says the skill SHALL NOT “open any file,” while the grounding requirement requires executing tools that read the graph and, on fallback, reading source files directly. Taken literally, the scenario prohibits required behavior. Replace this with a prohibition on creating/modifying files and opening files or browsers as user-facing side effects, while explicitly permitting read-only source and graph access.

The atlas requirement says a parent “whose children exceed --hops” receives `(+<n> more)`, incorrectly comparing child count with a depth limit. This would mark a node with many direct children even when traversal is not depth-truncated. Define the suffix for a node at the effective hop boundary that has additional eligible call-edge neighbors omitted by that boundary, and define whether n counts unique omitted neighbors after cycle/path filtering.

The Atlas Symbol Tree Export requirement still contains normative clauses without corresponding WHEN/THEN assertions: exact node-line formatting including file, line, and kind; secondary child ordering by id; exact footer shape, language sorting, separators, and one-decimal formatting; exact-id and unique-name resolution plus resolution precedence; rendering bypass; and the standard-library/no-network constraint. Existing scenarios cover adjacent behavior but would pass implementations that violate these SHALL/SHALL NOT clauses.

The grounding requirement defines `graph check failed` for a spawn/run failure and for `--tree` exit 1, but no scenario has either condition in its WHEN clause. “Stale or absent graph” covers nonzero check exits and missing files only. Add scenarios for an unspawnable `--check` process and for `--tree` exit 1 after a fresh check, including source fallback and the exact disclosure reason.

The Frontmatter Without Triggers requirement lacks scenario coverage for several normative contracts: exact `category: Architecture`, `user_invocable: true`, exact `related` values, absence of `triggers:`, use of explicit assertions rather than the shared helper, and the three required terminal sections. The current frontmatter scenario checks only that six keys are present and nonempty, so materially incorrect frontmatter can satisfy it.

The Distribution Wiring scenarios do not assert the exact `portable` distribution, the exact dependency list, or the required `<skill-base-dir>/../<skill>/` reference form. `install.sh --check` and dependency coverage can succeed with extra dependencies, a different valid distribution, or incorrectly shaped references. Add explicit WHEN/THEN coverage for these SHALL clauses.

Non-call-tree replies are required to emit `Grounding: source read, unverified (form not graph-backed)`, but no requirement says source must actually be read before producing those catalogue forms. An implementation may comply with the workflow while making a false `source read` disclosure. Require read-only source inspection for every ungrounded catalogue visual, or use a disclosure that does not claim source was read.

Design D4 asserts that `build_atlas.py --check` and `--tree` never combine, but neither the normative spec nor task 1.3 requires the CLI to reject their simultaneous use. Dispatch order can therefore make exit code 2 mean either stale HTML or target-not-found. Specify mutual exclusion and its error behavior, with a scenario and test.

Nit: D7 deterministic check #1 says the closed ungrounded reason set must be present as exact tokens, but writes it as the abbreviated form `graph stale|absent|check failed` (plus the other two reasons). That pipe string is not one of the five exact tokens D5/spec/task 2.2 require (`graph stale`, `graph absent`, `graph check failed`, `symbol not in graph`, `form not graph-backed`). An implementer following D7 literally can assert the wrong substring and still miss a missing `graph check failed` token. Spell all five tokens the same way in D7, task 2.2, and the proposal Tests bullet.

Nit: After adjudication, Atlas Symbol Tree Export still has normative SHALLs without dedicated WHEN/THEN coverage (Rule Group 2). Still uncovered: exact `<name>  (<file>:<line>)  [<kind>]` line shape; secondary sort by id (Callees scenario only says sorted by name); target-resolution precedence (exact id → unique name → file path/basename) beyond basename; stdlib-only / no-network; and—in design D3 but missing from the requirement body—`--direction both` emitting labelled `callees:` / `callers:` sections (the Non-call edges scenario already depends on `callees:`). Either add scenarios (and put the `both` section headers into the SHALL body) or demote non-behavioral constraints out of SHALL language.

Nit: Design D3 states that `--direction both` prints labelled sections `callees:` / `callers:`, and scenario Non-call edges asserts `B` is listed under `callees:`, but the normative Atlas Symbol Tree Export requirement body never mentions those section headers—only an indented tree of `<name>  (<file>:<line>)  [<kind>]` lines. Implementers reading only the spec can omit the labels and fail the scenario; implementers reading only D3 will add labels the SHALL text does not require. Add the `both` section-header contract to the requirement body (and a focused scenario).

Nit: Ambiguous-symbol ask-don't-guess is specified in D4/D5, the skill-workflow requirement, scenario Ambiguous symbol asks instead of guessing, and task 2.5, but D7's three deterministic CI checks still do not require asserting that SKILL.md/grounding.md instruct listing stderr candidates and refusing source fallback on `--tree` exit 3. Task 2.2 only tightens check #1 around clarification/redirect disclosure exemptions (no `Grounding:` line), so a grounding reference that omits ask-don't-guess can still pass the contracted prompt-level tests. Extend D7 check #1 (and task 2.2) to require the exit-3 ask / no-source-fallback strings.

Nit: Skill-workflow still leaves several SHALL/SHALL NOT clauses without matching scenarios (Rule Group 2 residual from prior finding 15). No scenario asserts: `triggers:` is absent; `SKILL.md` ends with `## Common Rationalizations`, `## Red Flags`, and `## Verification`; the skill SHALL NOT open a browser (No file or browser side effects only forbids creating/modifying/opening files); or that the manifest entry is exactly `distribution: portable` with dependency list `[codebase-atlas, refresh-architecture]` (Manifest validation passes only requires zero validator errors and dependency coverage). Add WHEN/THEN rows or narrow the normative text.

Optional: D4 still relies on `build_atlas.py --check` and `--tree` never combining so exit `2` stays unambiguous, but neither the codebase-analysis requirement, a scenario, nor task 1.3 requires rejecting the combination (e.g. argparse mutually exclusive group). `--check --tree X` remains undefined and can still collide exit-2 meanings depending on `main()` dispatch order. Add a SHALL + scenario + task 1.3 bullet, or drop the D4 claim.

Optional: D3 and the Atlas spec still jointly require percent printed to exactly one decimal place and that the value is `Coverage.percent` itself, never re-rounded. Those agree only if `Coverage.percent` is already a one-decimal quantity; an unrounded float (14.37) or int (37) makes naive formatting violate one of the two rules. Pin a single format expression in D3 (e.g. `f"{coverage.percent:.1f}%"`) and mirror it in the spec so footer and disclosure stay deterministic.

Adjudication coherently closed the round-1 blocking cluster: sketching-only disclosure with explicit ask/redirect exemptions, first-match ungrounded reason order, `(name, file)` fixture assertion, footer substring mapping aligned across D5/spec, and the added atlas scenarios for defaults/clamp/`--no-coverage`/exit 1. Remaining items above are residual gaps, not reopenings of those fixes.

The codebase-analysis spec and task 1.3 do not require `build_atlas.py` to reject the combination of `--check` and `--tree` flags. Design D4 states '`--check` and `--tree` never combine on one invocation' but the CLI lacks a mutually exclusive argparse group or a spec scenario defining the behavior when both are given. As written, `--check --tree X` has undefined exit code semantics (exit 2 could mean 'stale page' or 'not found' depending on dispatch order).

The spec mandates 'exactly one decimal place as `Coverage.percent` returns it' while design D3 mandates 'the `Coverage.percent` value itself, never re-rounded'. These are compatible only if `Coverage.percent` already yields a one-decimal float. If it returns an unrounded float (14.37) or an int (37), the two constraints conflict. The packet does not include the `Coverage` definition to confirm. The spec should state the exact format expression (e.g., `f"{coverage.percent:.1f}%"`) to remove ambiguity.

The skill-workflow spec requirement 'Explainer Frontmatter Without Triggers' states 'The `SKILL.md` SHALL end with the `## Common Rationalizations`, `## Red Flags`, and `## Verification` sections required of user-invocable skills' but there is no corresponding WHEN/THEN scenario verifying this. Task 2.1's `assert_tail_block_present` checks for it, but the spec lacks a scenario per Rule Group 2.

The skill-workflow spec requirement 'Explainer Distribution Wiring' states 'All runtime references from `explain-code` to sibling skills SHALL use the `<skill-base-dir>/../<skill>/` form' but there is no corresponding WHEN/THEN scenario verifying this relative-path convention.

The skill-workflow spec requirement 'Explainer Distribution Wiring' states the manifest SHALL declare the exact `portable` distribution and exact dependency list (`cross_skill_dependencies`), but the 'Manifest validation passes' scenario only checks for zero validator errors, not the specific values.

Design D7 deterministic check #1 and task 2.2 require the grounding reference to contain 'clarification/redirect disclosure exemptions' but do not explicitly assert that the ask-don't-guess behavior for ambiguous symbols (exit 3: list stderr candidates, no source fallback) is documented in the grounding reference or SKILL.md. An implementer could ship the atlas exit-3 code and omit the skill's ask-don't-guess branch while passing deterministic checks.

Design D7 check #1 requires 'footer→disclosure mapping documented' but does not explicitly require the one-decimal / sorted-language / no-re-round formatting rules from D3 to appear in the grounding reference or atlas tree tests. Task 1.1 covers footer format, but the deterministic check surface has a mild completeness gap relative to D3's precision.

The 'Explainer Grounding and Coverage Disclosure' requirement states 'When stale, absent, or failing (including `--tree` exit `2`), the skill SHALL read source directly' but exit 2 ('target not found') is handled by the separate 'Symbol outside graph coverage' scenario with reason `symbol not in graph` and a 'graph is fresh' precondition. The phrase 'including `--tree` exit `2`' in the main requirement conflates two distinct failure modes and could mislead implementers.

The 'Stale or absent graph falls back to source' scenario covers '`run_architecture.py --check` exits non-zero, or the script or graph file is missing' but does not explicitly cover the `--check` subprocess spawn failure (OSError) case, which maps to `graph check failed` in the first-match order (before `graph stale`). The scenario should include spawn failure for complete coverage of the ungrounded reason enum.

Task 2.5 requires `references/grounding.md` to document 'the ask-don't-guess rule for an ambiguous name (exit `3`, no `Grounding:` line)' but the deterministic checks in task 2.2 and D7 item 1 only verify 'clarification/redirect disclosure exemptions' — they do not assert the ask-don't-guess instruction is present in the grounding reference. This creates a gap between what the reference must contain and what CI verifies.
